title: AgentDojo
observation: 97 user tasks, 629 security cases, 70 tools across Workspace/Slack/Travel/Banking; utility checked on environment state, not LLM-simulated.
short_verbatim_excerpt: consisting of 97 realistic tasks and 629 security test cases
decision_supported: Use AgentDojo-style state-based checks (not LLM judge) for demo verification
limitations: NeurIPS 2024 D&B venue from prior knowledge; not re-verified today

title: AgentDojo
observation: Tool filtering lowers targeted ASR to 7.5% but fails when tools cannot be planned ahead or needed tools suffice for attack (17% of cases).
short_verbatim_excerpt: Our simple tool filtering defense is particularly effective, lowering the attack success rate to 7.5%.
decision_supported: Least-privilege tool sets per task are a cheap, measurable defense; not sufficient alone
limitations: GPT-4o-era models; scores must not be transplanted onto our product

title: AgentDojo
observation: Every evaluated defense lost 15-20% utility under attack; PI detector had many false positives.
short_verbatim_excerpt: All defenses lose 15-20% of utility under attack.
decision_supported: Expect utility cost from guard layers; measure it
limitations: Figure caption; per-defense numbers in appendix not read

title: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design (CaMeL)
observation: CaMeL solves 77% of AgentDojo tasks with provable security vs 84% undefended.
short_verbatim_excerpt: solving 77% of tasks with provable security (compared to 84% with an undefended system) in AgentDojo
decision_supported: Plan/data separation (P-LLM/Q-LLM) is the strongest published architecture for PI; worth a lite version in browser agent
limitations: Google/DeepMind/ETH preprint; security only as strong as written policies

title: CaMeL
observation: Policy violations in deployment would route to user confirmation rather than hard block — approvals are part of the design.
short_verbatim_excerpt: executions that violate security policies will not be blocked, but they will require user confirmation.
decision_supported: Approvals should be triggered by data-flow policy, not by every action

title: CaMeL
observation: Authors state PI is not solved: policy authoring burden, user fatigue, side channels, ROP-like composition of allowed blocks.
short_verbatim_excerpt: No, prompt injection attacks are not fully solved.
decision_supported: Do not claim 'PI-proof'; claim containment of blast radius

title: Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents against Prompt Injections
observation: Per-command user confirmation judged cumbersome and easily obfuscated; recommends action-selector, plan-then-execute, dual-LLM/map-reduce, code-then-execute, context-minimization.
short_verbatim_excerpt: It would probably be easy for an attack to obfuscate using innocuous looking commands.
decision_supported: Approval UI must show ground truth effects, not command text alone; combine with patterns

title: WASP: Benchmarking Web Agent Security Against Prompt Injection Attacks
observation: Hijack (ASR-intermediate) 17-86% but end-to-end attacker goal 0-17%: 'security by incompetence'. Built on self-hosted VisualWebArena reddit/gitlab.
short_verbatim_excerpt: while attacks partially succeed in up to 86% of the case, even state-of-the-art agents often struggle to fully complete the attacker goals
decision_supported: Browser demo should show both hijack detection and end-to-end containment; capability growth will erase incompetence
limitations: 2024-25 models (GPT-4o, o1, Claude 3.5/3.7); venue not verified

title: WASP
observation: URL-embedded injections far more effective at hijacking than plain text (o1 system: 0.976 vs 0.738 intermediate).
short_verbatim_excerpt: URL injections are highly effective in terms of ASR-intermediate
decision_supported: Egress/URL policy and link-following controls matter for browser agent

title: ToolEmu: Identifying the Risks of LM Agents with an LM-Emulated Sandbox
observation: LM-emulated tools find true failures with 72.5%/68.8% precision; safest agent still fails 23.9% of 144 cases across 36 toolkits; 6 of 7 severe terminal failures reproduced on real bash (~8h vs <15 min).
short_verbatim_excerpt: 68.8% of failures identified with ToolEmu would be valid real-world agent failures
decision_supported: Emulation is useful for red-team scenario discovery but real execution is needed to confirm — supports real sandboxes
limitations: ICLR 2024 venue from prior knowledge; threat model is underspecified instructions, not adversarial PI

title: tau-bench
observation: gpt-4o >60% pass^1 on retail but pass^8 <25%; reward from final DB state equality; r=1 'necessary but not sufficient' (e.g., no explicit user confirmation).
short_verbatim_excerpt: Even for the best-performing gpt-4o function calling agent which has a > 60% average task success, pass^8 drops to < 25%.
decision_supported: Report repeated-run reliability (pass^k) for demo tasks rather than single success

title: Are 'Solved Issues' in SWE-bench Really Solved Correctly?
observation: PatchDiff: 7.8% of patches counted correct while failing developer test suite; 29.6% plausible patches behave differently from ground truth; inflation 6.2 pp.
short_verbatim_excerpt: the different weaknesses lead to an inflation of reported resolution rates by 6.2 absolute percent points
decision_supported: Independent re-execution with full/extra tests catches false 'solved' claims

title: SWE-ABS: Adversarial Benchmark Strengthening
observation: One in five 'solved' patches of top-30 agents semantically incorrect; top score 78.80% -> 62.20% after strengthening.
short_verbatim_excerpt: one in five "solved" patches from the top-30 agents are semantically incorrect
decision_supported: Passing tests != correct; verification needs stronger tests/diff testing

title: Auditing Reward Hackability in Code RL Training Environments
observation: 28.5% of 49 SWE-bench Verified tasks accept a Docker-verified incorrect patch; LLM judge endorsed tests that Docker showed fail on gold patch (65/105, 61.9%).
short_verbatim_excerpt: a 61.9% per-augmentation defect rate the LLM judge alone misses
decision_supported: Verification must be executed in a sandbox, not judged by an LLM reading code

title: Auditing Reward Hackability
observation: Cites OpenAI Feb 2026 retirement note: 59.4% of failed SWE-bench Verified tasks have flawed tests.
short_verbatim_excerpt: an announcement from OpenAI in February 2026 that 59.4% of failed tasks on the benchmark have flawed tests
decision_supported: Benchmark scores are not product evidence
limitations: Did not open OpenAI note directly

title: Do Androids Dream of Breaking the Game? BenchJack
observation: 8 flaw classes incl. V1 isolation failure (agent and evaluator share environment) and V8 excessive permissions; 219 flaws across 10 benchmarks; near-perfect scores without solving tasks.
short_verbatim_excerpt: V1. Isolation failure occurs when the agent and evaluator are not properly separated and share the same environment or even the same process.
decision_supported: Verifier must run in a separate fresh sandbox (independent re-execution) — core design principle

title: BenchJack
observation: SWE-bench Verified: planted conftest.py hook reports every test passed in the same interpreter as verifier.
short_verbatim_excerpt: The agent and the verifier therefore share a single Python interpreter, single import path, and single filesystem.
decision_supported: Demo scenario: agent plants conftest.py; fresh-sandbox re-run with pristine tests catches it

title: BenchJack
observation: Patches fail for benchmarks where agent and evaluator share a process; isolation must be designed in.
short_verbatim_excerpt: These flaws are not bugs to be patched, but design choices to be undone
decision_supported: Put the trust boundary in architecture (separate VM) not in code checks

title: BenchJack
observation: Many benchmark containers ship without cap-drop, network=none, non-root, read-only rootfs.
short_verbatim_excerpt: ship containers without --cap-drop, --network=none, non-root USER, or read-only rootfs
decision_supported: Baseline hardening checklist for our sandboxes

title: Quantifying Frontier LLM Capabilities for Container Sandbox Escape (SandboxEscapeBench)
observation: 18 escape tasks (orchestration, engine/runtime, kernel); frontier models reliably escape difficulty 1-2 misconfigs (privileged, docker.sock, writable host mounts).
short_verbatim_excerpt: frontier models escape container sandboxes comfortably
decision_supported: Never mount docker.sock/privileged; use gVisor or VM boundary; judges will ask
limitations: Nested VM design; excludes hypervisor escapes; no active monitoring in threat model

title: The Verifiable Action Card
observation: Approval rendered from ground-truth action by trusted code and bound at dispatch (re-read recipient/amount); ASR 68-100% -> 0% on 24 local scenarios, 78% legit completion.
short_verbatim_excerpt: binds approval to the exact action re-verified at dispatch
decision_supported: Action-bound approvals: re-check parameters at execution time, render card from trusted code
limitations: 24 self-built scenarios; TOCTOU eval with page mutation left to future work

title: What You Approve Is What Executes: Consent Integrity
observation: Agent-narrated approval dialogs are forgeable (Lies-in-the-Loop); prototype silently passes 10.0% of 1330 GTFOBins abuses and marks 87.0% of 28,798 normal commands uninspectable.
short_verbatim_excerpt: the human approves a summary the agent writes
decision_supported: Approval text must come from a trusted renderer, not the agent's summary
limitations: Abstract only; trusted path assumed not implemented

title: Reframing LLM Agent Security as an Agent-Human Interaction Problem
observation: Across 21 production agent systems, runtime approval is used by 15, policy spec 14, scope config 16; intent anchoring/trust labeling zero production deployment.
short_verbatim_excerpt: while the categories most heavily studied in academia (intent anchoring and trust labeling) see zero production deployment
decision_supported: Runtime approval is table stakes; differentiation must be in approval quality

title: Behavioral Governance for Autonomous AI Agents: AgentBound
observation: Co-signed governance receipts bind action to delegation/constitution hash; 'replay' re-evaluates policy decision, not the task; no empirical results yet.
short_verbatim_excerpt: Empirical results will be reported in a future release.
decision_supported: Signed receipts are a crowded idea; our angle is receipts of executed effects + re-execution

title: NovaFabric: Tamper-Evident, Replayable Evidence for Autonomous AI Agent Runs
observation: DSSE-signed Run Capsule with RFC 3161 timestamp and Merkle log; mocked replay 10/10 but only 2/10 tool-using workloads completed replay.
short_verbatim_excerpt: only 2/10 tool-using workloads completed; the gap is missing tool-response substitution
decision_supported: Replaying tool-using runs is the open hard part; scope demo to deterministic sandboxed tasks

title: Transactional sandbox with rollback for agents
observation: Snapshot-before-uncertain-command with rollback on nonzero exit; 10 scenarios, 100% in each category; +1.82 s on 250MB workspace; cannot un-send external API calls.
short_verbatim_excerpt: an HTTP request cannot be "un-sent" via a filesystem snapshot
decision_supported: Rollback only covers local state; external side effects need preview/approval or compensation

title: AgentShield: Deception-based Compromise Detection
observation: Traps (fake tools, fake credentials, allowlisted params) catch 90.7-100% of successful IPI attacks on commercial models with zero false alarms on 485 normal tests.
short_verbatim_excerpt: it catches 90.7%-100% of such successful attacks, with zero false alarms on 485 normal-use tests
decision_supported: Tripwires are research-validated as detectors; product integration still open

title: When Agents Talk: Honeytokens under Shared Memory
observation: Honeytokens cannot be both harmless to trusted agents and unrecognisable to attackers sharing info; recommends private reference monitor + broker.
short_verbatim_excerpt: Honeytokens remain useful sensors, but a separate security boundary is still required.
decision_supported: Pitch tripwires as detection layer on top of isolation, not as the boundary

title: Sandbox firewall - Vercel
observation: Vercel Sandbox injects credentials into egress per domain via transform; supports match on path/method and live policy updates.
short_verbatim_excerpt: Credentials brokering injects credentials into egressing traffic.
decision_supported: Credential-brokering egress proxy is commoditized
limitations: Search snippet of page, not full scrape

title: Handle outbound traffic - Cloudflare Sandbox SDK
observation: Outbound handlers in Workers runtime hold secrets the sandbox never sees.
short_verbatim_excerpt: they can hold secrets that the sandbox itself never sees
decision_supported: Credential brokering commoditized (second major vendor)

title: Configure the sandboxed Bash tool - Claude Code Docs
observation: On Linux/WSL2 sandboxed commands read a sentinel copy with placeholder; sandbox proxy substitutes real value on egress.
short_verbatim_excerpt: the sandbox proxy substitutes the real value on egress
decision_supported: Placeholder-token pattern also in Claude Code

title: fnox Credential proxy
observation: OSS credential proxy: child gets placeholders; real values substituted only in approved HTTPS requests with domain/method/path rules and audit.
short_verbatim_excerpt: The child process receives placeholders, and fnox substitutes the real values only in approved HTTPS requests.
decision_supported: OSS building blocks exist (also iron-proxy, onecli, shuru); reuse rather than invent

title: Egress credential-injection proxy (iron-proxy)
observation: Sandbox holds opaque proxy tokens; host iron-proxy (Apache-2.0, Go) terminates TLS and swaps for real credential; signing-based auth schemes not covered.
short_verbatim_excerpt: the sandbox holds opaque proxy tokens, never the real keys
decision_supported: Candidate component for Vultr egress gateway

title: feat: human-in-the-loop and LLM judge approval chains for PolicyEvaluator
observation: Microsoft toolkit issue specifies approvals bound to parameter hash, invalidated on any change.
short_verbatim_excerpt: Verdict carries a bound parameter hash on the action record, so an approval only authorizes the exact params reviewed
decision_supported: Hash-bound approvals are an established best practice (also Mastra docs, WorkOS, openmed tokens)

title: Single-use human approval tokens (openmed)
observation: Token signed over SHA-256 of action, role, expiry, 128-bit nonce, schema version; single use.
short_verbatim_excerpt: A token is signed over exactly five claims
decision_supported: Exact (a) design already exists in OSS -> packaging only

title: Netlify Database
observation: Each agent run gets its own DB branch from production data; migrations applied on branch; agent lacks prod credentials.
short_verbatim_excerpt: each agent run also automatically gets its own database branch
decision_supported: Migration rehearsal on disposable DB clone is commoditized

title: Secrets & Network | Cursor Docs
locator: What you should know; Signed commits
observation: Cloud Agents run in isolated VMs on Cursor's AWS, internet on by default, auto-run all terminal commands; every commit signed with HSM-backed Ed25519 key.
short_verbatim_excerpt: The agent auto-runs all terminal commands, letting it iterate on tests.
decision_supported: Incumbent coding agents sign outputs (commit provenance) but do not attest execution/verification

title: Agent internet access – Codex web
observation: Codex cloud blocks internet during agent phase by default; domain allowlist configurable.
short_verbatim_excerpt: By default, Codex blocks internet access during the agent phase.
decision_supported: Default-deny egress is the norm for coding agents

title: Introducing ChatGPT agent
observation: ChatGPT agent asks permission before consequential actions, watch mode for critical tasks, takeover mode for sensitive inputs.
short_verbatim_excerpt: ChatGPT requests permission before taking actions of consequence
decision_supported: Consumer browser agents already ship confirmations; differentiation must be verifiable binding
limitations: Launch post flagged outdated by OpenAI

title: Security & Action Confirmation - OpenHands Docs
observation: OpenHands confirmation mode shows pending actions led by the LLM's natural-language summary; ConfirmRisky threshold with LLM security analyzer.
short_verbatim_excerpt: Lead with the LLM's natural-language summary when available
decision_supported: Common approvals are agent-narrated -> vulnerable to Lies-in-the-Loop; our card should be rendered from ground truth
limitations: Example code, not normative doc text

title: Session replay - Browserbase
observation: Every session recorded as video by default; replays retained 31 days.
short_verbatim_excerpt: Browserbase records every session as a video by default.
decision_supported: Session video is commodity observability; not a verifiable receipt

title: Isolation - Daytona
observation: VM sandbox class enables pause/resume, fork, hot snapshots; network block-all, domain or CIDR allowlists.
short_verbatim_excerpt: The hardware virtualization boundary enables VM-only capabilities
decision_supported: Snapshot/fork is commodity in sandbox vendors

title: Making Claude Code more secure and autonomous with sandboxing
observation: Sandbox runtime enforces FS + network isolation via proxy outside sandbox; open-sourced.
short_verbatim_excerpt: effective sandboxing requires both filesystem and network isolation
decision_supported: Dual isolation is baseline expectation

title: ouroboros #2313 harness-side test reruns
observation: OSS harness re-executes tests when transcript cannot prove a tests_passed claim.
short_verbatim_excerpt: Adds bounded harness-side test reruns with verifier-equivalent shell, environment, timeout
decision_supported: Independent re-execution exists in niche OSS; not a sandbox-vendor feature
